source.title: Synthetic continued pretraining
source.authors: Zitong Yang; Neil Band; Shuang-Ping Li; Emmanuel J. Candès; Tatsunori Hashimoto

record.tranche_reason: The study measures downstream QA accuracy as synthetic training-token count varies, a different measure and setting from held-out cross-entropy scaling.
record.gate_note: The paper does not measure held-out pretraining loss or sweep model parameters or compute. It reports downstream QA scaling with synthetic token count, and a separate scaling comparison on summarization false claims. Results cited from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: Its own continued-pretraining runs on an 8B model measure downstream QA accuracy as synthetic training-token count grows, and report a log-linear trend. That bears on V6 in a new setting: small-corpus synthetic continued pretraining. It does not measure held-out loss, so V1–V5 and V7 are untouched. T3 fits better than T2 because the question is the same but the training regime and data axis differ.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that EntiGraph synthetic CPT shows consistent, log-linear scaling of closed-book QA accuracy up to 455M synthetic tokens. Raw-document CPT shows no improvement and paraphrase CPT asymptotes early. EntiGraph CPT yields over 80% of RAG's accuracy gain and composes with both RAG and instruction tuning. A toy model gives a mixture-of-exponentials scaling form that closely fits the empirical curve, which the authors attribute to the toy model; the record wrongly calls it the authors' scaling formula derived from data.
record.recipe_differences: Measures downstream QA accuracy and summarization after synthetic continued pretraining, primarily against synthetic token count; it does not measure held-out cross-entropy across parameter, data, or compute scales.
record.method_sensitivity: The observed QA scaling differs by synthetic-data method: EntiGraph, rephrasing, raw-document CPT, and task-specific QA SFT have different reported trends. The summarization comparison also varies short versus long prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: A toy graph-memorization model predicts that link density grows as a mixture of exponentials in synthetic-generation rounds. The curve has linear, log-linear and plateau phases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In entity-graph synthetic augmentation, knowledge acquisition grows as a mixture of exponentials and plateaus at the deductive closure of the source data.

record.problems: Evidence is limited to one 8B model and one small-corpus benchmark. The study measures downstream accuracy rather than held-out loss and does not vary parameter count or compute. The token-count accuracy curve is described qualitatively between its reported endpoints; numerical uncertainty for that curve is not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant scaling results were left out. RAG comparisons and general summarization comparisons without a scale variation were omitted.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss; no parameter or compute sweep.
No small-run fits extrapolated to larger runs.
No allocation of parameters versus tokens at fixed compute.
Loss is never measured, so the power-law form in continued pretraining or fine-tuning is not tested. The fitted form is a mixture of exponentials on accuracy, not a loss power law.
Untested parts: downstream performance against pretraining loss; scaling in parameters or compute; out-of-sample prediction of larger runs from the fitted curve; more than one model or corpus.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents.

missing.what: Empirical fit of QA accuracy to synthetic tokens (in millions): y = 64.5456 − 13.8352·0.9989^x − 8.4705·0.8961^x − 3.932·0.0546^x. It implies an accuracy asymptote near 64.5%, i.e. a predicted plateau rather than continued log-linear growth.

record.verdict_notes: Evidence comes from a single 8B model and a single corpus (QuALITY). The axis scaled is synthetic continued-pretraining tokens, not pretraining parameters or compute. Rows R2, R3, R6 and R7 are baselines or method comparisons, not scale results. The study is not an original source for any version.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or parameter, token, or compute power-law measurements.
No small-run loss fits used to predict much larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep over parameter count and token count.
No architecture comparison at fixed parameter count.
The paper studies synthetic continued pretraining, but does not test whether the claimed held-out-loss power law transfers to this or other training regimes.

Tests QA accuracy against synthetic token count for one model and one corpus, plus a summarization comparison; does not test downstream performance against pretraining loss or across parameter/compute scaling.
Does not test dependence of held-out-loss exponents or compute-optimal allocation on setup or fitting choices.

rows.subject: EntiGraph CPT
rows.operation_detail: Continually pretrained on randomly subsampled EntiGraph synthetic corpora of varying token counts.
rows.value: 56.22% after continued pretraining on 455M tokens; accuracy is described as scaling log-linearly with token count up to 455M
rows.note: The paper reports the endpoint and trend in text; intermediate curve values are shown in the figure.

rows.subject: Llama 3 8B Base
rows.operation_detail: Measured on the closed-book QuALITY QA evaluation without continued pretraining on the target corpus.
rows.note: Reference accuracy for the trained-model comparisons; by itself it does not measure improvement with scale.
rows.check: Base-model reference accuracy (39.49%), not a scale result. It is the baseline already given in R1, so it should not be a separate V6 row.

rows.subject: Raw CPT
rows.operation_detail: Continually pretrained on the original 1.3M-token Raw QuALITY corpus.
rows.note: The paper says Raw CPT performs worse than the base model.
rows.check: Raw CPT is a single tuned run on the 1.3M-token corpus (4 epochs) with no variation in data scale. Falling below base (38.15% vs 39.49%) is a method comparison, not evidence about scaling, so 'reversed' for V6 is wrong.

rows.subject: Rephrase CPT
rows.operation_detail: Repeatedly trained on synthetic paraphrases generated with three rephrasing prompts.
rows.value: figure only; described as scaling poorly relative to EntiGraph, with a slower scaling trend
rows.note: The text reports the qualitative comparison; no exact accuracy value is given.
rows.check: Accuracy rises with paraphrase tokens up to 38M but more slowly, and the conclusion says it asymptotes early. Figure-only values; partial is correct.

rows.subject: QA SFT
rows.stage_stated: continued pretraining on synthetic QA pairs
rows.operation_detail: Trained on generated question-answer pairs and evaluated at varying synthetic token counts.
rows.value: figure only; text describes a very sharp improvement in QA accuracy
rows.note: The paper says QA SFT reaches high performance, and EntiGraph attains similar performance while being task-agnostic.
rows.check: Task-specific QA SFT up to 28M tokens shows a sharp accuracy rise with tokens. Figure-only; it is a task-specific comparator, not the main method.

rows.subject: EntiGraph-29M Instruct
rows.stage_stated: continued pretraining on 29M EntiGraph tokens, then instruction tuning
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated as the token-matched smaller-scale model in the summarization comparison.
rows.measure: false claims relative to human summary
rows.note: Figure 8 includes this condition; the text describes lower false-claim counts for full-scale EntiGraph compared with the 29M model.
rows.check: The 29M-token condition is the baseline for R8, not a separate result. Fold it into R8.

rows.subject: EntiGraph toy model
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed toy graph-memorization link density as synthetic-data generation rounds increase.

conditions.value: directed Erdős–Rényi graph model; Figure 5 uses V = 100 and p = 0.03

rows.measure: link density, used by the authors as an analogue of QuALITY accuracy
rows.value: Theoretical mixture-of-exponential form, with fast growth, slower growth, and plateau phases
rows.note: This is a toy-model analysis, not a held-out loss or a measured downstream task result.

relationships.condition: EntiGraph synthetic CPT of Llama 3 8B, closed-book QuALITY QA, 1.3M source tokens expanded to up to 455M synthetic tokens
relationships.reason: Accuracy rises from 39.49% to 56.22% and is described as log-linear in token count across random subsamples (R1). A three-term exponential mixture fits the curve in-sample, but it is never used to extrapolate.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy rises from 39.49% to 56.22% approximately linearly with log token volume, with an exponential-mixture curve fitted without extrapolation.

relationships.condition: EntiGraph Instruct, closed-book summarization, short and long prompts
relationships.reason: Going from 29M to 455M tokens significantly reduces false claims for both prompts. Only two scale points are compared, so this shows improvement rather than predictability (R8, R9).
relationships.display_finding: Increasing synthetic pretraining from 29M to 455M tokens significantly reduces false claims under both short and long summarization prompts.

relationships.condition: Synthetic CPT on repeated paraphrases (Rephrase) instead of diverse entity-based data
relationships.reason: Downstream accuracy grows more slowly and asymptotes early by 38M tokens. Gains with data scale depend on the data's diversity, not on token count alone (R4).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy grew more slowly and approached a plateau by 38M tokens, showing that data diversity affected gains beyond token volume.
